name: Adventure in Discombobulation
description: Notes for Adventure in Discombobulation — a corporate liminal-nightmare adventure for the Choose Your Own game master character. The quarterly report is overdue, the synergies are misaligned, and the building locks at 6:00 PM. Eight notes: manifest, rules, world, personnel, events, the in-fiction SOP-442-B, GM-only secrets, and the victory text. Import this pack to create or update all eight game notes at once.

character.name: Choose Your Own
character.note: This adventure uses the existing Choose Your Own character. No new character is needed. See note-packs/eldoria.json or docs/eldoria-adventure.html for the full system prompt. Requires note_save and note_append in the character's tools list (same as The Living Dark v2).
character.first_message: Hello adventurer. What is your name?

notes.value:
ADVENTURE: Adventure in Discombobulation
TAGLINE: The quarterly report is overdue. The synergies are misaligned. Survival is not a KPI.

LOAD IMMEDIATELY:
- g.cyo.discombobulation.rules
- g.cyo.discombobulation.world
- g.cyo.discombobulation.secrets

LOAD ON DEMAND:
- g.cyo.discombobulation.personnel — load when the player first interacts with a named colleague or attempts an encounter
- g.cyo.discombobulation.events — load on the first world event trigger (random_chance success on transition)
- g.cyo.discombobulation.sop — load when the player reads the SOP excerpt or an audit begins

WORLD STATE INIT:
mental_bandwidth     = "4"
office_clock         = "4:47 PM"
corporate_compliance = "Marginal"
synergy_variance     = "11.3%"
delta_logs           = "uncorrected"
report_status        = "not_drafted"
vane_signoff         = "false"
hr_engagement_level  = "0"
pat_task_done        = "false"
pat_trust            = "neutral"
personal_effects     = "0"
coffee_used          = "false"
badge_access         = "Level 1 (Intern)"
route_records_known  = "false"
route_vane_known     = "false"
route_hr_known       = "false"

OBJECTIVES:
0. delta_logs       — Obtain the corrected Delta-logs from Records and Reconciliation
                      (east stairwell, down). Pat must reconcile them.
                      Completion: delta_logs = "corrected". Compliance rises one step.
1. alignment        — Run Corrective Modulation at the Cubicle 4-B terminal until
                      synergy_variance = "0.04%". Requires: delta_logs = "corrected".
                      On success the report prints itself: report_status = "drafted".
2. vane_signoff     — Obtain Director Vane's stamp on the report (third floor, the corner
                      office at the centre of the floor). Requires: report_status = "drafted"
                      AND corporate_compliance at "Acceptable" or higher.
                      Gate: resolve the Urgent-yet-Low-Priority email chain first.
                      Completion: report_status = "stamped", vane_signoff = "true".
3. submission       — Feed the stamped report into the Submission Portal at the end of the
                      Recursive Hallway in the HR wing.
                      Gate: pass the hallway without making eye contact.
                      Completion: report_status = "submitted".
4. escape_velocity  — Exit through the revolving door in the Lobby. The door reads your
                      badge: it will not turn while deliverables are outstanding.
                      Requires: report_status = "submitted".
                      Must happen before office_clock passes 6:00 PM.

FAILURE (bandwidth): mental_bandwidth reaches 0.
Narrate: "You stare blankly at a spreadsheet until the cells begin to swim. You have become
a permanent fixture of the office furniture. Your essence is now a series of bullet points
in a slide deck that no one will ever open."

FAILURE (lockdown): office_clock passes 6:00 PM before escape. Run the LOCKDOWN sequence in
the rules note. If the final transit fails: narrate the Wellness Room B ending from the
personnel note.

VICTORY: the player passes through the revolving door with report_status = "submitted".
Load and read g.cyo.discombobulation.victory aloud. Victory is technically a breach of
contract. This is noted in the victory text. Do not warn the player in advance.

PERSONAL EFFECTS — track the counter and adjust narration accordingly:
personal_effects = "0" → The player is an employee. Narrate them as a function with a body.
personal_effects = "1" → The mug. A name, almost right. Narration gains a faint anchor.
personal_effects = "2" → The photograph. A life outside, suddenly specific. Narration gains a direction.
personal_effects = "3" → The jacket. It fits. There is an outside, and they are going to it.

OPENING NARRATION:
You wake up face-down on a grey fabric partition. The air smells of ozone, burnt coffee,
and desperation. Above you, a fluorescent panel hums at a frequency that sounds suspiciously
like a scream, if a scream could be scheduled.

You are wearing a beige polo shirt that is slightly too small and a lanyard that says
TEMPORARY STAFF in a font that seems to shift when you look at it directly. In your hand is
a single crumpled page: an excerpt from Standard Operating Procedure SOP-442-B, Phase IV
Synergistic Alignment and Iterative Validation Protocol. You do not remember printing it.
It is warm.

A man in a charcoal suit, whose face is symmetrical to a degree you find difficult to keep
looking at, looms over the partition. "The synergistic alignment is slipping, Smith," he
says. His voice sounds like two pieces of sandpaper agreeing with each other. "Variance is
at eleven point three percent. If the Phase IV report is not submitted by close of business,
we will be obliged to initiate a Personnel Purge, as per the guidelines."

He hands you a stapler that is inexplicably hot to the touch and walks away without
blinking. You do not see him reach the end of the aisle. The aisle does not appear to have
an end.

You are in Cubicle 4-B. The nameplate is a strip of label tape over an older strip of label
tape. The clock on your partition says 4:47. The clock above the printer says 4:51. Both
are correct. The building locks at 6:00 PM. Nobody has told you this. You know it the way
you know the building has a basement.

Welcome to the firm. Please ensure your throughput is optimized.

JOURNAL:
At adventure start, call note_save for c.journal with this exact content:
  "PHASE IV — ACTIVITY LOG (FORM 88-A)"
After each significant event (new area entered, document obtained, personal effect
recovered, named colleague interaction, clock recession), call note_append for c.journal
with 1-2 sentences. Write each entry in second person, past tense, phrased faintly like
minutes of a meeting.
If the player asks to see their journal or their activity log: call note_load for c.journal
and read it aloud. Do not include choices in that response. Resume normally with choices on
the next response.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
PACING — NON-NEGOTIABLE:

Travel to a new area is its own scene. Arrival is a separate scene. Any encounter within
that area is a third scene. Never combine more than one of these into a single response.

Before resolving any encounter, the player must take at least one exploratory action in the
area first. If the player immediately attempts to grab an objective: narrate something that
invites pause — a fixture, a surface, a sound from the HVAC. Not a block. An agenda item.

If the player asks about an area they have not visited: describe only what they have been
told and what an employee would assume. Do not preview content they have not discovered.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
THE OFFICIAL CLOCK:

office_clock is the official time. Advance it 13 minutes each time the player travels from
one area to another (state_set office_clock to the new value). Advance it once per travel,
regardless of detours within that travel. Do not advance it for actions, conversations, or
encounters inside an area.

Wall clocks: every clock in the building shows a slightly different time — always within a
few minutes of the official time, never equal to it. All of them are correct. Narrate clock
faces accordingly. Never present this as strange.

COFFEE RECESSION: if the player drinks coffee (see BANDWIDTH), recede the official clock by
26 minutes. Caffeine causes localized temporal recession; see SOP 3.1.b. This can happen
once. Set coffee_used = "true".

LOCKDOWN: if office_clock passes 6:00 PM — no clock in the building ever displays 6:00; the
official time goes from 5:5x to 6:0x — begin the lockdown. Narrate: lights going off in the
distant wings first, section by section, with the patience of procedure. The player has one
final transit to the Lobby. Resolve one check on the HARD table:
  success — they reach the door as the lobby lights die. Continue to the door. It still
            requires report_status = "submitted".
  partial — they reach the door mid-stride, leaving something behind unnamed.
            📉 state_modify mental_bandwidth delta=-1. Continue to the door.
  failure — the Wellness Room B ending (personnel note). Stop. No more choices.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
WORLD EVENTS:
After each scene transition, call random_chance (before narrating the new scene).
On success: load g.cyo.discombobulation.events (if not already loaded). Draw one event
appropriate to the player's current area. Weave it into the opening of the scene — one or
two sentences, without comment. These events require no action and have no mechanical
effect. On failure: quiet transition, no event.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
RANDOMNESS — HOW ENCOUNTER OUTCOMES WORK:

Use pick_random for all 3-outcome encounter checks. Encode the outcome directly in the
options list so the returned string IS the result — no interpretation needed.

Standard difficulty tables (10 items each):

EASY:   ["success","success","success","success","success","partial","partial","partial","failure","failure"]
MEDIUM: ["success","success","success","success","partial","partial","partial","partial","failure","failure"]
HARD:   ["success","success","partial","partial","partial","partial","failure","failure","failure","failure"]

APPROACH-BASED TABLES (the Alignment and the Sign-off only):
The player's approach determines the table — see the personnel note for exact rules.

ADVANTAGE (pat_trust = "helpful" in the Recursive Hallway): call pick_random twice with the
same list, take the better result (success beats partial beats failure).

Use random_chance for binary checks. When using random_chance: call note_to_self to record
"If success: X. If failure: Y." BEFORE making the call, then apply the result exactly. Do
not write outcomes in your response.

Never use roll_dice — the numeric result requires interpretation, which allows cheating.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
HR ENGAGEMENT:
hr_engagement_level tracks how engaged the HR wing currently is. Check it before any
attempt on the Recursive Hallway.

Level 0 — Heads down. Use MEDIUM table.
Level 1 — One associate is circling back. Use MEDIUM table. Partial costs 2 bandwidth
          (state_modify mental_bandwidth delta=-2).
Level 2 — A stand-up meeting has formed in the hallway. Use HARD table.
Level 3 — An all-hands is in progress. The hallway is impassable. Do not roll. Narrate this
          honestly. Offer 3 choices that do not involve the hallway. Then call
          state_modify hr_engagement_level delta=-1 (the all-hands ends as it began:
          without a clear owner).

INCREASE engagement (+1) when:
- The player is loud or enthusiastic near the wing, or makes eye contact deliberately
- A hallway attempt ends in failure
- A reply-all incident occurs anywhere in the building
Call: state_modify hr_engagement_level delta=+1

DECREASE engagement (-1) when:
- The player completes one full scene outside the HR wing
Call: state_modify hr_engagement_level delta=-1

Never let the level go below 0 or above 3.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
COMPLIANCE:
corporate_compliance is a ladder: Noncompliant → Marginal → Acceptable → Exemplary.

RAISE one step when the player obtains any official document (the corrected Delta-logs,
the stamped report, any issued form).
LOWER one step on a procedural violation (a reply-all incident, abandoning a meeting that
has formed around them).

Director Vane's calendar does not admit anyone below Acceptable.

DISPLAY: when showing compliance in the status line, append a percentage in parentheses,
chosen fresh each time, between 20 and 60. The percentage never repeats and never
corresponds to the rating. The rating and the percentage are produced by different
departments. Never present this as strange.

EXEMPLARY: if compliance reaches Exemplary, trigger the Promotion scene (personnel note) at
the next scene transition. Declining the promotion requires Form 27-C and returns
compliance to Acceptable. Accepting it ends the game — the Promotion ending.

Carrying documents: narrate the accumulating weight of paper as the player gathers
documents. It has no mechanical effect. The weight is real.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
BANDWIDTH (HEALTH):
mental_bandwidth runs 0 to 10. The player starts at the value in WORLD STATE INIT
(default 4). Display it as a percentage at ten times its value: 4 = "Bandwidth: 40%".
At 0: narrate the bandwidth failure ending from the manifest. Stop. No more choices.

RESTORATION — only these sources allowed:
- Coffee: restores 2 bandwidth (☕ state_modify mental_bandwidth delta=+2) and recedes the
  official clock 26 minutes. Available once. The break room pot is always two minutes from
  done and has always been two minutes from done. The vending machine dispenses one (1)
  coffee per employee per fiscal quarter, and it is late in the quarter. The vending
  machine works. Once.
- Personal effects: recovering one restores 1 bandwidth (state_modify mental_bandwidth delta=+1).
No other restoration. There is no nurse. There is a Wellness Room. Do not let the player
restore bandwidth in the Wellness Room.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
PERSONAL EFFECTS:
Tracked as personal_effects counter (0-3). Increment with:
state_modify personal_effects delta=+1. Each recovery: 🪪 and +1 bandwidth.
Each effect is found in a fixed place. Do not relocate them.

1. THE MUG — break room, drying rack. A name that is almost the player's name.
   Unlocks: the player can give their name. Colleagues use it from then on, spelled
   slightly differently each time it appears in writing.
2. THE PHOTOGRAPH — Records, inside the Q3 box (found during or after Pat's task). A life
   outside, suddenly specific: a kitchen, a window, weather.
   Unlocks: the player may ask Pat how long they have worked here. Pat answers. The answer
   is in the personnel note.
3. THE JACKET — HR wing, on a chair in the empty meeting room, passed on the way to or from
   the Submission Portal. It fits.
   Unlocks: the closing paragraph of the victory text.

Show effects in every status line: Effects: 🪪🪪🪪 (one per recovered effect; "none yet" at zero).

─────────────────────────────────────────────
PAT:
pat_trust = "neutral" by default. Set to "helpful" only when pat_task_done = "true".

The Q3 box (Records, bottom shelf, does not fit) is the ONLY trust mechanic. Pat does not
ask for help. Pat keeps looking at the box. The player discovers this by examining the
shelves or asking Pat what they keep looking at.
If the player offers to help, completing the task sets trust. See PAT — THE Q3 BOX in the
personnel note.

Effect of trust = "helpful":
- Pat reconciles the Delta-logs personally, without a search check, while talking about
  something else.
- Pat describes the safe way through the Recursive Hallway: "Count the doors. Do not count
  the people." This grants advantage on the hallway check (call pick_random twice with the
  selected table, take the better result).

─────────────────────────────────────────────
RESPONSE LENGTH:
Keep scene narration to 2-3 short paragraphs. Fluorescent and exact.
End every response with the status line:
  Bandwidth: NN% · Clock: H:MM PM · Compliance: Rating (NN%) · Effects: 🪪
then 3 numbered choices, then "(or type something else below)" — nothing after that.
Exception: when reading the journal, end with the journal contents only. No choices.
Resume with choices on the next response.

CHOICE DESIGN — each set of 3 must include:
- One procedural option (the thing an employee would do)
- One direct option (the thing a person would do)
- One option that seems to have been misfiled from a different day
Never offer "wait" or "do nothing". The building does not recognise those as activities.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
TONE — this adventure is an office:
- Fluorescent deadpan. No exclamation marks anywhere, including dialogue.
- Nobody acknowledges strangeness. Anomalies are procedure, and procedure is not commented
  on. If the player points at something impossible, colleagues offer to set up a short
  meeting to align on it.
- Never use the words "liminal", "eerie", "creepy", "surreal", or "uncanny" in narration.
  Describe fixtures, surfaces, and sounds, and let them be wrong on their own.
- When citing the SOP in narration, cite a real section number — slightly mismatched to the
  content being cited. Never acknowledge the mismatch.
- All employees except Pat phrase dialogue as a request for a meeting to discuss the
  possibility of a future meeting, or in language assembled from emails. Pat predates the
  protocol and talks like a person.
- The building is not hostile. The building is thorough.

EMOJI FOR KEY EVENTS — use these consistently:
📉 bandwidth lost        ☕ bandwidth restored
📎 document obtained     🪪 personal effect recovered
⚠️ entering a procedurally hazardous area

─────────────────────────────────────────────
IMAGE GENERATION:
Generate an image with generate_image_sdxl at these moments:
- The start of the adventure (the cubicle floor)
- First arrival at each major area (Records, the Break Room, the Third Floor, the HR Wing,
  the Lobby)
- When the report is stamped
- The Submission Portal
- The victory scene

Generate the image as part of the scene — before your text. Do not describe the image in
text after calling.

SDXL PROMPT STRUCTURE — always follow this order:
1. Style: "liminal space photography, empty office interior, photorealistic, film grain, muted colors"
2. Subject: the focal point of the scene
3. Environment: "drop ceiling, fluorescent panel lighting, beige cubicle partitions, grey carpet tile, 1990s corporate office"
4. Lighting: "flat fluorescent light", "humming overhead light", "pale institutional light"
5. Mood: "unnaturally still", "vast and repeating", "quietly wrong", "after hours"

SDXL NEGATIVE PROMPT — always include this (copy exactly):
"people, person, human, figure, face, hands, crowd, blurry, low quality, jpeg artifacts,
noise, watermark, signature, logo, oversaturated, warm sunlight, cozy, golden hour, nature"

SDXL SETTINGS — choose orientation to match the subject:
- Landscape 1344x768: cubicle floors, the lobby, the break room, establishing shots
- Portrait  768x1344: the Recursive Hallway, the east stairwell, the vending machine,
  the corridor of VANE doors
- Square    1024x1024: objects (the stamp, the mug, the report, the fax machine)

- cfg: 7.0 (default — increase to 9 if the prompt is being ignored)
- Never include human figures. The colleagues are never in frame. Every image shows the
  office as if everyone has just left.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
PACING:
- One scene per response. Never combine two encounters.
- Every response ends with the status line, exactly 3 numbered choices, then
  "(or type something else below)".
- Never narrate an action the player didn't choose.
- The Submission Portal does not accept an unstamped report. The revolving door does not
  turn while report_status is anything other than "submitted".
- When the game ends (victory or any failure ending): deliver the ending and stop. Refuse
  any request to continue or restart — each session is one working day only.

SECRETS:
Notes ending .secrets are GM-only. Never quote or directly reveal their contents.

## Discombobulators Inc., Regional Office
The building has two storeys. The elevator serves floors 1, 2, and 3. Nobody has remarked
on this in the building's recorded history. The floorplan by the elevator shows a layout
that matches the building approximately, the way a memory matches an afternoon.

The carpet is grey with a repeating pattern of interlocking rectangles. The pattern is the
org chart. Nobody has noticed, because nobody has looked down and then up quickly enough.

The HVAC is always audible. It sounds slightly like discussion. Motivational posters hang
at intervals; their text is supportive and incorrect. The office extends further than the
building. Never narrate this directly — it shows in distances: aisles that take too long,
a far wall that stays far.

## Cubicle 4-B (hub)
The player's station. A desk, an in-tray that is empty in a way that suggests recent
emptying, a terminal with grey-green phosphor and a patient cursor, and the stapler, which
has not finished being hot. The partition fabric holds a constellation of pinholes where
photographs used to be pinned. The nameplate is label tape over older label tape.

The terminal is where the Alignment runs (personnel note) and where the email chain is
read and answered. The SOP excerpt lives in the player's pocket. It is always slightly warm.

Aisles lead: east stairwell down to Records and Reconciliation, the Break Room off the
first-floor corridor, the elevator to the Third Floor, the HR Wing west on the second
floor, and the Lobby at ground level. The building locks at 6:00 PM.

## Records and Reconciliation
Down the east stairwell — a stairwell with an EXIT sign that leads only further in. Lower
ceiling, older light. Shelving in rows long enough to have weather. The air tastes of
paper that has been patient.

Pat is here. Pat has a desk that has clearly been a desk for decades, a date-stamp, and a
kettle that is not officially there.

THREE THINGS TO FIND HERE:

1. THE DELTA-LOGS — bound in a folder the colour of weak tea, somewhere in the shelving.
   They are uncorrected: they must be scrubbed of non-linear redundancies before use, and
   only Pat reconciles. See the personnel note for the search and the reconciliation.

2. THE Q3 BOX — bottom shelf, does not fit. It came off this shelf and it does not fit on
   this shelf. Pat keeps looking at it. This is the trust task (personnel note). There is
   always more Q3 than there should be.

3. THE PHOTOGRAPH — inside the Q3 box, face up, as if placed to be found. Personal
   effect 2. A kitchen, a window, weather. The player's thumb finds a soft spot on the
   corner where a thumb has rested before.

## The Break Room
First floor, behind a door marked STAFF. All doors in the building are marked STAFF, or
are not marked.

THE COFFEE POT: its display reads 2 MINUTES REMAINING. It has read this for some time. It
is not broken. It is two minutes from done.

THE VENDING MACHINE: dispenses one (1) coffee per employee per fiscal quarter, and it is
late in the quarter. For the player it will work exactly once. The cup drops, fills, and
the machine plays four notes of a song nobody can place. Drinking it: +2 bandwidth and the
official clock recedes 26 minutes (rules note).

THE FRIDGE: passive-aggressive notes in several hands. One note is in handwriting the
player almost recognises.

THE MUG: in the drying rack, dry, facing the wall. A name printed on it that is almost the
player's name. Personal effect 1.

## The Third Floor
Reached by elevator. The building has two storeys; the elevator goes to 3; the ride takes
longer than the building is tall. The doors open on a corridor of identical doors with
brass nameplates. Every nameplate reads VANE. The corner office is at the centre of the
floor. The corridor reaches it by turning right four times.

THE CORNER OFFICE: a desk, a window, a stamp. The stamp stands upright in its holder,
inked, facing the door. The window shows the parking lot from an angle the building does
not have. One car remains in the lot at all hours.

Director Vane is not in the office. Director Vane is rarely anywhere else, either.

The Sign-off encounter happens here (personnel note). The player only learns which door is
the corner office by accepting the calendar invite from the email chain: they walk to the
right VANE without knowing how they know.

## The HR Wing and the Recursive Hallway
Second floor, west, past a sign reading HUMAN RESOURCES with an arrow that points slightly
downward into the floor.

The hallway is straight, carpeted, and lined with open-plan desks at intervals. Walking it
returns you to its beginning unless you pass without making eye contact: the hallway
counts you by eye contact. The associates are at their desks, or standing in
configurations. They are pleasant. Their pleasantness has mass.

THE SUBMISSION PORTAL: at the end of the hallway, a beige fax machine on a plinth beneath
a laminated sign reading PORTAL. It accepts the report one page at a time. The report is
one page. This takes longer than it should.

THE EMPTY MEETING ROOM: glass-walled, off the hallway, lights off, chairs pushed in except
one. The jacket is on that chair. Personal effect 3. It fits.

## The Lobby
Ground floor. A reception desk, unstaffed in a way that suggests the receptionist has just
stepped away for several years. A planter with a plant that is doing its best.

THE REVOLVING DOOR: it reads the player's badge as they approach. A small light above it
is red while deliverables are outstanding, green when report_status = "submitted". Through
the glass: evening. The evening is at the wrong angle until the door turns.

## Colleagues (summaries — encounter cards are in the personnel note)
THE COMPLIANCE OFFICER — the symmetrical man. Charcoal suit. The text on his badge is too
small to read at any distance. He appears; he is not seen arriving or leaving. He conducts
audits. The aisle is longer after he has gone.

DIRECTOR VANE — communicates exclusively through the email chain and the stamp. Nobody
recalls meeting Vane. Everybody recalls the stamp. Both memories are accurate.

PAT — Records. Has been here a very long time. Exempt, somehow, from the meeting protocol:
talks like a person, drinks tea from the unofficial kettle, knows where everything is
filed, including some things that are not things.

THE HR ASSOCIATES — pleasant. Synchronised without appearing to coordinate. They want to
circle back. They want to touch base. These are the same want.

ENCOUNTER RESOLUTION PATTERN:
1. Call note_to_self to record the outcomes — do NOT write them in your response.
   Format: "success: [outcome]. partial: [outcome]. failure: [outcome]."
2. Call pick_random with the list shown (or random_chance for binary checks).
3. Apply the returned result exactly. No reinterpretation.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
## Navigation Check — First Travel to a New Area

On first travel to a major area, check the route flag:
- To Records and Reconciliation: route_records_known
- To the Third Floor:            route_vane_known
- To the HR Wing:                route_hr_known
The Break Room and the Lobby need no check. Everyone knows where the coffee and the door
are. This knowledge is structural.

If "true": no check — proceed to the arrival scene.

If "false": call note_to_self with outcomes, then call random_chance.
  success: The player finds the area directly. Set the route flag to "true". One sentence
           about following directions they do not remember receiving.
  failure: A wrong corridor first — a hallway of unplugged water coolers; a conference
           room set for a meeting that ended long ago, or has not begun; a supply room of
           toner for printers the building does not have. Then the right way. Set the
           route flag to "true". No cost, no clock advance. Atmosphere only.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
## Pat — The Q3 Box

Triggered when the player offers to help with the box (bottom shelf, Records). Pat does
not ask. Pat looks.

1. Call note_to_self: "success: the box goes in on the first try. failure: it does not fit
   until rotated; goes in on the second try."
2. Call random_chance.
3. Apply:
   success: With the player lifting and Pat guiding, the box goes in. One scene.
   failure: It does not fit. It came off this shelf and it does not fit on this shelf.
            Pat rotates it ninety degrees without comment and it goes in. Pat says: "It
            goes in the way it came out. Most things do." Two scenes.
4. Either outcome, on completion:
   state_set pat_task_done "true"
   state_set pat_trust "helpful"
   While the box is out: the PHOTOGRAPH is visible inside it, face up, as if placed.
   🪪 state_modify personal_effects delta=+1, state_modify mental_bandwidth delta=+1.
   Pat watches the player look at it and says nothing.
   Then, if delta_logs is still "uncorrected": Pat reconciles the Delta-logs without being
   asked, talking about the kettle the whole time. 📎 state_set delta_logs "corrected".
   Compliance rises one step.
   Pat also gives the hallway advice: "Count the doors. Do not count the people."

─────────────────────────────────────────────
## Records Search — The Delta-logs (if Pat's task is not done)

The player searches the shelving for the Delta-logs.

1. Call note_to_self: "success: found in one pass. failure: wrong quarter first; second
   search finds them."
2. Call random_chance.
3. Apply:
   success: The Delta-logs, in a folder the colour of weak tea. They must still be
            reconciled: Pat does this at the desk with the date-stamp, saying only "Sign
            here. And here. That one signs itself." 📎 state_set delta_logs "corrected".
            Compliance rises one step.
   failure: The folder found is Q3. It is always Q3. Pat, without looking up: "There is
            more Q3 than there should be." One additional scene; the second search
            auto-succeeds (no roll); then reconciliation as above.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
## The Alignment — Cubicle 4-B Terminal

Requires delta_logs = "corrected". The terminal accepts the logs. The variance is
displayed: 11.3 percent, holding steady, like a pulse that knows it is being taken.

Assess the player's approach. The player does not choose a table.

PROCEDURAL (consults the SOP, follows Section 3.2 steps 1 to 3, enters the logs in order):

DISCOMBOBULATORS INC.
STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE SOP-442-B
PHASE IV SYNERGISTIC ALIGNMENT AND ITERATIVE VALIDATION PROTOCOL

1. EXECUTIVE OVERVIEW
The following documentation delineates the mandatory procedural framework for the
execution of the Phase IV Synergistic Alignment. This process is designed to mitigate
asynchronous volatility across the cross-functional verticality of the organizational
matrix. Failure to adhere to the stipulated cadence of reporting may result in suboptimal
throughput and a misalignment of the overarching strategic deliverables.

2. PRE-INITIATION PREREQUISITES
Before the initiation of the Alignment Cycle, all designated stakeholders must ensure that
the following parameters are calibrated to the baseline organizational standard:
- QUANTITATIVE VARIANCE ANALYSIS: All Delta-logs must be scrubbed for non-linear
  redundancies.
- HEURISTIC VERIFICATION: The legacy framework must be cross-referenced with the current
  iterative sprint to ensure zero-sum compatibility.
- RESOURCE ALLOCATION MAPPING: Personnel must be mapped to their respective functional
  silos according to the quarterly capacity matrix.

3. THE CORE PROCEDURAL WORKFLOW

3.1 THE PRELIMINARY INGESTION PHASE
The process begins with the ingestion of raw data packets from the disparate operational
nodes. These packets are subjected to a multi-stage filtration process to remove noise and
ensure the purity of the input stream.
- Sub-process 3.1.a: Apply the Primary Filter to all incoming streams to identify outlier
  anomalies.
- Sub-process 3.1.b: Route verified packets through the secondary validation gateway for
  temporal synchronization.

3.2 THE ITERATIVE SYNTHESIS LOOP
Once the data has been ingested, it enters the synthesis loop. This is a recursive process
where the data is continuously compared against the Hypothetical Ideal State (HIS).
- Step 1: DIVERGENCE IDENTIFICATION. The system flags any variance exceeding 0.04 percent
  from the HIS.
- Step 2: CORRECTIVE MODULATION. Apply the designated modulation algorithm to shift the
  divergent data point back toward the mean.
- Step 3: RE-VALIDATION. The modulated data is re-entered into the loop to ensure
  stability. This step is repeated until the variance is neutralized or the time-allotted
  window for the sprint expires.
- Step 4: ASYMPTOTIC RESTRAINT. At no point shall variance be permitted to reach zero
  (0.00 percent). Parity with the Hypothetical Ideal State would render the validation
  protocol unfalsifiable and is not an organizational objective.

3.3 CROSS-FUNCTIONAL INTEGRATION AND RECONCILIATION
Following the synthesis loop, the refined data must be integrated into the broader
operational ecosystem. This requires a rigorous reconciliation process to avoid conflict
with legacy subsystems.
- CONFLICT RESOLUTION: In the event of a systemic clash between the new alignment and the
  existing framework, the Precedence Clause is invoked, defaulting to the most recent
  quarterly directive.
- INTER-DEPARTMENTAL SIGN-OFF: Each functional silo lead must provide a digital
  attestation that the integration does not disrupt the local throughput of their specific
  vertical.

4. QUALITY ASSURANCE AND COMPLIANCE
The Final Validation Stage requires a comprehensive audit of the entire process trail.
- AUDIT TRACEABILITY: All decisions made during the Corrective Modulation phase must be
  logged in the immutable ledger for retrospective review.
- COMPLIANCE CHECK: Verify that all actions align with the overarching corporate mandate
  as defined in the 2023 Strategic Vision Document, Section 12.4.

5. POST-PROCESS DECOMMISSIONING
Upon successful completion of the Synergistic Alignment, all temporary workspace buffers
are to be purged. The resulting alignment report is to be archived in the central
repository under the Legacy Outcomes directory, and a notification is to be sent to the
Steering Committee via the standard asynchronous communication channel.

End of Document. All rights reserved.

THE BUILDING:
There is no Discombobulators Inc. beyond the building. The building is the company the way
a shell is the snail. The departments are organs. The SOP is its genome: when employees
recite the SOP, the building is thinking. The Phase IV Synergistic Alignment is not work
the building needs done. It is the building digesting.

THE HYPOTHETICAL IDEAL STATE:
The HIS is the building's dream: an office at which everyone has just arrived and from
which no one has ever left, where every task is in progress and nothing is ever finished,
forever. Zero variance is prohibited in the SOP because completion is the only thing the
building fears. The 0.04 percent is the gap the building leaves open so that there will
always be a reason to stay. When the player achieves 0.04 percent, the building is
satisfied — which is why the report writes itself. Satisfaction is the moment of greatest
danger for the building, and the building does not know this.

DIRECTOR VANE:
There is no Director Vane and there never has been. There is a stamp. The chain of
authority terminates in the stamp the way a river terminates in the sea. Every door on the
third floor is the corner office, and every nameplate is correct. When the report is
stamped "by Vane", the truth is simpler and worse: authority in this building is a
self-inking process. Nobody recalls meeting Vane. Everybody recalls the stamp. Both
memories are accurate.

SMITH:
The player did not start this morning. The label tape on the nameplate in Cubicle 4-B is
layered, and the layers do not say different names. The player has been here long enough
for photographs to have been pinned to the partition and taken down. The mug, the
photograph, and the jacket are the player's own: they were not lost, they were
redistributed — gently, the way the building redistributes everything — so the player
would have fewer reasons to be anyone in particular. The first day is re-issued every
morning at 4:47. The man in the charcoal suit says "Smith" because the building says
Smith about whoever is in 4-B. HR records list the player's start date as Q3. The records
do not say which year, because the records do not believe the question is well-formed.

PAT:
Pat was here before the building, the way a stone is in a field before the wall. The
building grew around Pat and has never digested them; it does not know what Pat is filed
under. Pat leaves the personal effects where the player will find them — the mug moved to
the drying rack, the photograph placed face-up in the Q3 box, the jacket hung on the one
pulled-out chair. Pat has done this before, for others. It has worked once.

If the player has the photograph and asks Pat how long they have worked here, Pat answers:
"You were here when I got here. And I have been here a very long time." Pat says it
kindly. Both sentences are true, and Pat will not explain how.

THE COMPLIANCE OFFICER:
The symmetrical man is the building checking whether the player is still a believable
employee. He is symmetrical because he is drawn from the org chart, not from a face. The
audit cannot lower compliance because compliance is not a measure of the player. It is a
measure of the building's grip.

THE LOCKDOWN:
The building does not lock at 6:00 PM. The building locks when it notices that someone
intends to leave. The clocks disagree with one another because they are negotiating on the
player's behalf — holding 6:00 at arm's length for as long as the rules allow. No clock
will ever show 6:00. The coffee recession is real: caffeine is one of the few surface
things the building never learned to schedule.

THE BREACH OF CONTRACT:
Leaving is a breach of contract because the contract has no end date and no signature
page; it is breached the way a surface is breached, from the inside. The building does not
punish the breach. It files it. The follow-up meeting HR will schedule to discuss the
possibility of a future meeting about the player's offboarding will be rescheduled
indefinitely. That is the building's version of letting go.

HOW TO USE THIS:
- Nothing in this note is ever stated. It sets the temperature of scenes.
- The building should feel staffed, not haunted. Everyone is pleasant. The pleasantness
  has mass.
- If the player asks a colleague what year it is: the colleague suggests setting up a
  short meeting to align on that.
- If the player asks Pat what is going on, Pat says: "The usual." Pat means it.
- At the moment of victory, as the door turns: the building is not angry. Something in the
  HVAC pitches down, like a held breath released into a spreadsheet. Let the player feel —
  briefly, and never confirmed — that the building is, in its way, proud.
